thread:
alex: heads up — hit a pretty confusing combo of issues when running the sample edge function with the new SDK build. getting overload/generic errors only in the edge runtime, but Node CJS works fine. anyone seen this?

maria: can you paste the error and tsconfig? small changes in moduleResolution helped us before.

alex: error log: ```ts
TS2345: Argument of type 'string | undefined' is not assignable to parameter of type 'T'.
  Type 'undefined' is not assignable to type 'T'.
at call (node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/index.d.ts:45:12)
```

alex: minimal example: overloaded client.create:
```ts
function create<T>(body: T): Promise<Response>
function create(body: unknown): Promise<Response>
```
call site: `client.create(user?.payload)` -> works in Node, errors in edge.

jordan: hmm. edge bundler likely inlines different d.ts resolution. what's your tsconfig?

alex: ```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2020",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "Node",
    "strict": true,
    "skipLibCheck": false
  }
}
```

sam: two things to check: 1) `skipLibCheck: true` for a quick unblock (dts mismatch), 2) try `moduleResolution: "Bundler"` or `"NodeNext"` depending on your toolchain. esbuild/tsup sometimes needs bundler mode for ESM types.

maria: also edge runtimes (Vercel/Cloudflare) use a different host for `lib.dom` and sometimes treat `unknown` vs `any` differently during inference. If your overloads rely on implicit `any` widening, that can break. Make generics explicit or narrow the union before calling.

alex: thanks. quick follow-up — auth+retry behaviour seems inconsistent too. in browser/edge, requests sometimes don't retry after 401->refresh flow. Node SDK auto-retries fine.

jordan: that's a known parity gap. browser/edge can't use background refresh with native fetch the same way. If your token refresh mutates a shared in-memory client, edge worker instances are ephemeral and may race. Workaround: return a promise from auth hook and use `client.withAuth()` on each incoming request. We should document this in the SDK samples.

sam: adding to that — make sure sample uses `fetch` polyfill only if you need it. Edge platforms provide fetch; polyfills can change behaviour (keepalive, signal).

alex: pulling fixes: changed tsconfig to `moduleResolution: "Bundler"`, set `skipLibCheck:true`, tightened overloads to accept `unknown` and then cast after null-check: `if (user?.payload == null) throw; client.create(user.payload as User)` — builds for edge now.

maria: can we make the sample app include a tiny helper utility `safeCall<T>(v: T|undefined, fn:(t:T)=>Promise<any>)` to encourage explicit null checks and avoid overload ambiguity?

jordan: yes, and file an SDK issue for dts parity. we should also add an entry in docs: "Edge runtime: tsconfig presets" with recommended settings for Next/Cloudflare/Vercel.

sam: deploy-bot: deploy failed for branch alex/edge-typing-fix — bundler error: Unexpected token 'export' in node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/index.cjs. :warning:

alex: argh — that's the other piece: we were importing the wrong entry. For edge/ESM, use `import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk/esm'` (or set `exports` conditions). For CJS, keep default. Will update sample to import conditional based on env.

maria: simple PR checklist: 
- add tsconfig presets for edge + node
- update sample imports for explicit esm entrypoint
- add note about auth refresh race and recommended `withAuth` pattern
- mark `skipLibCheck` recommendation as temporary and open dts fix issue

alex: filing the issue now and pushing sample PR. thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks — can someone from docs + devex review once PR is up? small changes will help a lot for new users hitting these gotchas.

jordan: noted, will review.
